halfLife.notes: Plasma half-life is short, but tranylcypromine irreversibly inhibits MAO-A and MAO-B. Clinical effect persists for 10–14 days after stopping until new enzyme is synthesised. Often considered more activating than phenelzine — used in atypical/refractory depression. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

activeMetabolite.notes: No clinically significant active metabolite for mood purposes. Some amphetamine-like metabolites contribute to the 'activating' clinical profile.

cypInteractions.switchingRelevance: Irreversible MAOI — same washout principles as phenelzine. 14-day washout required before any serotonergic agent. Tyramine-rich food crisis risk identical to phenelzine. Tranylcypromine has additional sympathomimetic activity, so caution with other indirectly-acting sympathomimetics. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

maoiWashout.notes: 14-day washout in either direction. Specialist supervision required for MAOI-to-MAOI switches (rare).

discontinuationSyndromeRisk.notes: Withdrawal (especially abrupt cessation in chronic users) can cause severe agitation, psychotic symptoms, cognitive impairment, and sympathomimetic withdrawal features. Taper slowly over 4+ weeks. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

formulationNotes: Limited availability in Malaysian formulary. Specialist supply only. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
